newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mostly up after early sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mostly up after early sell-off.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures bounced back from steep early losses to finish mostly higher in volatile trading Tuesday, boosted by chart-driven speculative and local buying, market sources said.
"Everyone who sold it, bought it back," one trader said. "There's no rhyme or reason to it. It's just a technical, wide-swinging market."
May futures closed up 3.15 cents per lb, to 194.30 cents, after ranging from 195.00 to 183.50. Second-position July rose 2.00 cents, to 176.15, while the back months finished up 2.00 to down 3.00.
The May/July switch, which narrowed early in the day to around 15.00 cents, ended at 18.15 cents, up from 17.00 cents at the close on Monday.

Speculative profit taking, led by commission houses, pressured the market from the outset, traders said. Downward momentum accelerated after the May contract slipped below 187.00 and 185.00 cents per lb, triggering sell-stops.
But roaster price-fixing emerged toward May's low of 183.50 cents, stemming the sell-off and preventing a test of chart support at 183.00 cents.
"It held the 183.00 support level and came rallying back," said Stephen Smith, president of South Futures in Miami. "After it got past unchanged, everyone jumped on it."
Although there was no fresh fundamental input today, Smith said the market's fundamental outlook remained supportive.

Low levels of consumer coffee stocks in the U.S., combined with the prospect of smaller Central American and Colombian crops in 1996/97, are expected to underpin coffee futures through the second half of the year.

Some dealers said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data, which showed non-commercial net long positions down to 5,307 lots as of March 25 compared with some 9,000 lots net non-commercial longs two weeks ago, indicated there was plenty of room for further speculative buying.
Additionally, a decline in coffee open interest to 37,435 lots as of March 31, from more than 42,000 lots a month ago, may also suggest speculators could beef up their positions.
"The CFTC tells me specs are not in the market as much as they could be," one dealer said, "which is also what the open interest tells me."

On the charts, some traders said the May contract appeared poised to test the 200.00 mark, with strong resistance noted at May's life-of-contract high of 209.50. On the downside, near-term support was seen around 192.00, then 190.00.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were down 250 60-kg bags, 83,328 bags as of March 31. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume reached an estimated 11,025 lots, nearly double Monday's official tally of 6,521 lots.
